summary: Round 7 is finished and recorded under '## Round 7' in /home/user/foundress/docs/design/tasks/colony-life-ledger.md. The first engineer's two fixes were already in the tree when I took over and I left them as they were: RM (the mound-mask restore fix; a save and load now continues the same game in 8 of 8 tests on playground-park #3) and SF3 (tenders leaving the nest together). I added three of the small owner-less seams from direction 12. The round went to protein, not year two. In the sweep-6 runs the queen lays about 11 eggs on hand-over day 1 and almost none after, while 26 P sits unused in the colonies' stores at winter and 25.5 P more is still held by six queens. The laying probe found the cause: the winter-reserve rule (WINTER_RESERVE_FROM_D28 = 10) shuts the protein supply to the queen on most warm hours after a start-day-5 hand-over. I tested two fixes on five colonies (one per archetype), each run to winter from the same sweep-6 hand-overs, and reverted both. L1 (move that rule to the start of autumn) did make the queen lay more eggs earlier, but those eggs cannot hatch into workers before winter. They used up the stored protein, the colony foraged harder and lost more workers to old age: 50 workers at winter against 56 (3 colonies worse, 2 equal). T1 (an unvisited egg or pupa pile outranks feeding larvae) made untended brood deaths worse (15 to 21) and turned the colony scenario test red. The round therefore ends with the base result on this subset: 56 against 56 workers, all 5 colonies equal. The next lever for year one is the number of nurses in small colonies, not the order of their jobs.
causesRanked: 1. Eggs not laid in the warm window while protein sits in store: 238 eggs in 15 sweep-6 runs, about 170 of them on hand-over day 1; 0-6 per run on days 2-6 although the queen could lay 15-37 eggs a day; at winter 26 P left in the stores and 25.5 P still held by 6 queens (about 40 larvae). The probes show the winter-reserve rule (viab-economy R5, from d28 10) is the only closed gate on gd 1.3-4. Paired runs then showed those eggs cannot become workers before winter after a start-day-5 hand-over, so this costs year-two brood, not year-one workers.

2. Brood lost in care: 34 eggs and 21 pupae died untended and 19 eggs drowned in sweep 6. In year one, only the day-1 batch becomes workers, so this is the lever there. Causes found: on suburban-garden #3, nurses stuck in a pocket of the nest the navigation does not reach (4.5 of 15.2 ant-days spent in the nest); on car-park-verge #3, one nurse working against a nurse demand of 1.4-3.6.
3. Protein income: median protein intake 0.197 of need, 1-8 P delivered per run; it limits the larvae of the day-1 batch (woodland-edge #1: 6 larvae starved).
4. Old age: 65 of 92 adult deaths. Workers age faster outside the nest, so more foraging trips mean more old-age deaths before winter (the R11 ruling stands).
